citations.desc: Attending veterinarian and adequate veterinary care (dealers and exhibitors).
citations.narrative:
Daily observation of a rabbit to assess its health and well-being is not being done adequately. One male rabbit, mostly
grey with brown fur above its eyes, had in both ears, from the ear canal extending to the opening, a moderate amount of
crusty flaky brownish red material. The skin beneath the material appeared pink and irritated. The licensee had not
identified this condition and therefore, has not communicated with the veterinarian. Failure to identify this health issue
delayed timely communication with the attending veterinarian and led to treatment delay, which may negatively impact the
health and well-being of this rabbit. The licensee must conduct thorough daily observations of all the animals to assess
their health and well-being, as well as maintain direct and frequent communication with the veterinarian so that timely and
accurate information on problems of animal health, behavior, and well-being is conveyed. The rabbit identified above
needs to be assessed by the veterinarian for a treatment plan.

The primary enclosure for eleven rabbits was not maintained to protect the animals from injury. At the time of inspection, a
long extension cord was actively powering a large fan within the enclosure and was accessible to the rabbits.
Approximately 10 feet of the extension cord was lying on the ground of the enclosure. The cord entered from the back left
side through the wire, ending where the fan was placed about halfway into the enclosure. Electrical cords pose a
significant health risk to animals that may bite or nibble on them. Primary enclosures must be constructed and maintained
so that they protect the rabbits from injury.
Correct by: 06/26/2026.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the licensee.
Additional Inspectors:
Stephanie Mayard, VETERINARY MEDICAL OFFICER n
